correction.prior_error: Circle Q2 2026 USD12.442B USDC on-platform and 19.5% daily weighted-average share were mislabeled as Coinbase metrics in the 08:31 graph addendum.
correction.corrected_claim: Those are Circle's own platform metrics. Coinbase Q3 average USD22B USDC in eligible products and USD8.616B AOP USDC at September 30 are separate metrics with different definitions and time bases.
correction.reason: Direct SEC filing definitions and Coinbase Q3 earnings-deck appendix were reconciled.
correction.preservation: Previous snapshot, graph and source records remain immutable; this addendum supersedes only the misattributed metric observation.

confirmed_facts.claim: Circle Q2 2026 USDC on-platform end balance was USD12.442B and daily weighted-average percentage was 19.5%. Circle defines this as its own platform, including Circle Mint, corporate-held USDC and Circle-provided non-custodial wallets.
Circle says the daily weighted-average percentage of USDC on its platform is used to calculate Circle's share of reserve income under the Collaboration Agreement.

Coinbase Q3 2026 average USDC held in Coinbase products reached USD22B, approximately 30% of average USDC market capitalization and 49% above the prior year; the metric includes corporate USDC and USDC held for customers in eligible Coinbase products.
Coinbase Q3 2026 AOP table reports USD8.616B USDC at September 30. AOP is a point-in-time measure of assets held/managed in platform digital wallets and custody, with customer-held-key exclusions.
Circle incurred USD324.6M Q2 and USD655.3M H1 2026 distribution costs under its agreements with Coinbase.
Coinbase Q3 stablecoin revenue was USD306.905M versus USD324.534M in Q3 2025; higher average USDC balances contributed USD84.6M while lower interest rates reduced revenue USD52.8M.
Circle SBI Japan K.K. is a direct 50/50 Circle-SBI JV for USDC distribution in Japan; SBI Holdings and SBI Shinsei Bank invested USD25M each in Circle at IPO.

inferences.claim: Coinbase and Circle remain economically interdependent through USDC distribution and revenue-sharing economics, while Coinbase diversifies into RLUSD and other stablecoins.
inferences.basis: Coinbase says its Circle arrangement was renewed on the same terms; Circle reports distribution costs under Coinbase agreements; Coinbase reports USD22B average USDC in eligible products.

inferences.claim: Coinbase's USD22B average eligible-product balance cannot be used as a direct substitute for the USD8.616B September 30 AOP balance or Circle's USD12.442B Circle-platform balance.
inferences.basis: Different definitions, scopes and measurement periods in the respective filings/deck.

unknowns: Coinbase's exact numeric share of Circle's total average USDC on-platform balances under the Collaboration Agreement is not disclosed in the cited Q2 2026 table.
The portion of Coinbase's USD22B average eligible-product USDC attributable to Hyperliquid and other off-exchange products versus custodial balances requires a product-level breakdown.
No transaction-level evidence yet links Circle/SBI or Coinbase USDC balances to native XRP purchases, collateral deposits or bridge usage.
Circle SBI Japan JV Q3 operating results and Japanese USDC distribution balances remain unavailable at this cutoff.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Circle says the Circle SBI Japan JV had no significant operating results through June 30, 2026.
Coinbase Q3 stablecoin revenue declined approximately 5.4% year over year despite higher average USDC balances, because lower rates offset part of the balance contribution.
Circle states the relationship between interest rates and USDC circulation is complex, highly uncertain and unproven.
